--- title: "[Graph.set_edge_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Set attribute values for one or more edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13144-L13333){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.set_edge_attrs( edge_attr, values, edge_ids=None, edges=None, sources=None, targets=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Set edge attributes](/assets/graphs/set-edge-attrs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Every edge of a six-node graph carries a value w on its label. The call names the edge B to E, drawn in a light accent stroke, which holds 4; after it that edge reads 5, in the accent color, while the other four edges keep their values." width="100%"} Writes a single named attribute onto edges, modifying the graph in place. The edges to update can be chosen in one of four ways: by edge ID (`edge_ids=`), by explicit `(source, target)` pairs (`edges=`), by filtering on endpoint nodes (`sources=` and/or `targets=`), or, if none of these is given, all edges. The same value can be broadcast to every targeted edge, or different values can be given per edge via a list or a dict. The attribute is created if it doesn't exist and overwritten if it does. Typical uses include: - assigning weights, capacities, or costs that later algorithms will read - tagging relationship types (e.g., `rel="friend"`) on a known set of edges - setting visual attributes such as edge color or width before plotting The name `"weight"` is special: it is stored as the edge's first-class weight (converted to a float) rather than as a generic attribute, which is what weighted algorithms use. To set attributes on the currently selected edges instead, see `set_edge_attrs_ws()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the attribute to set (e.g., `"weight"`, `"rel"`, `"color"`). This becomes a column of the same name in `get_edge_df()`. Using `"weight"` updates the edge weight itself. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any | list[Any] | dict[int, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The value(s) to write. Three forms are accepted: - a **dict** mapping edge IDs (`int`) to values. Only targeted edges whose ID is a key are updated; the others are left unchanged. Keys are edge IDs, not node pairs. - a **list** of values paired by position with the targeted edges. Its length must equal the number of targeted edges. The order is that of `edge_ids=` when given; for the other targeting options it follows internal edge order, so passing `edge_ids=` is the safest way to use a list. - **any other value** (a string, number, tuple, `None`, etc.), which is written to every targeted edge. [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of edge IDs to update. Takes precedence over all other targeting options. An ID that doesn't exist raises a `KeyError`. Default is `None`. [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of `(source, target)` tuples, where each endpoint is a node ID or label. Every edge between each pair is updated (including parallel edges); in undirected graphs a pair matches in either orientation. Pairs that refer to unknown nodes, or that have no edge between them, are silently skipped. Ignored if `edge_ids=` is given. Default is `None`. [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels; only edges leaving these nodes are updated. Can be used alone or combined with `targets=`, in which case an edge must satisfy both. Unknown nodes are silently skipped. Ignored if `edge_ids=` or `edges=` is given. Default is `None` (no restriction on the source). [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels; only edges entering these nodes are updated. Can be used alone or combined with `sources=`. For undirected graphs an edge matches in either orientation, so `targets=["A"]` selects every edge touching `A`. Unknown nodes are silently skipped. Ignored if `edge_ids=` or `edges=` is given. Default is `None` (no restriction on the target). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `values=` is a list whose length doesn't match the number of targeted edges. [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `edge_ids=` contains an ID that does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The simplest way to target edges is by edge ID. Here the first two edges of a 4-node path get an explicit weight, and the third edge (which has none) is absent from the result: ::: {#8cfd6841 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids())[:2] graph.set_edge_attrs("weight", 2.5, edge_ids=edge_ids) graph.get_edge_attrs("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 2.5, 2: 2.5} ``` ::: ::: Omitting all targeting options applies the value to every edge, and a list assigns a different value to each edge by position: ::: {#1df2700c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.set_edge_attrs("status", "active") graph.set_edge_attrs("priority", [1, 2, 3], edge_ids=list(graph.get_edge_ids())) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 7)
idsourcetargetrelprioritystatusweight

``` ::: ::: `(source, target)` tuples are often more readable than edge IDs when the endpoints are already known: ::: {#6c2ecf4c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.set_edge_attrs("rel", "friend", edges=[("A", "B"), ("C", "D")]) graph.get_edge_attrs("rel") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 'friend', 3: 'friend'} ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph, `sources=` picks out every edge leaving the given nodes. Here both of the hub's outgoing edges are marked, while the incoming edge from `X` is not: ::: {#a4f44553 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Hub", "X", "Y", "Z"]) .add_edges([("X", "Hub"), ("Hub", "Y"), ("Hub", "Z")]) ) graph.set_edge_attrs("outbound", True, sources=["Hub"]) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
